newsitem.title: USA: US to probe McDonnell Douglas China deal - NYT.
newsitem.headline: US to probe McDonnell Douglas China deal - NYT.

text.p: A U.S. federal grand jury is investigating whether aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas Corp or the Chinese government knowingly violated U.S. export-import laws in a $1.6 billion order for 40 airplanes, the New York Times reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said the criminal inquiry was trying to find out if McDonnell Douglas and the procurement arm of the Chinese Aviation Ministry broke a U.S. export law after signing a $5 million side agreement for the sale of machine tools two years ago.
It said McDonnell Douglas sold the tools for a future factory that would build a new kind of aircraft.
China never built the factory and instead sent the tools to a military factory that made missiles and other weapons, it said.
The newspaper said China's move broke the rules of the export license set by the U.S. Commerce Department.
After the department complained about the breaking of its license rules, China sent the tools to a joint venture installation with McDonnell Douglas in Shanghai, it said.
The newspaper said McDonnell Douglas had insisted that it found out about the move and alerted the department in March 1995.
But government officials said the company might or should have known about it beforehand.
The inquiry is trying to determine whether McDonnell Douglas and China knowingly misled the department to get approval for the export.
